This surah was devoted to promise, threat, and warning, and it suffices as admonition for whoever understands it.

His saying ﴿diverts you﴾ means: occupies you in a way for which you have no excuse. Diversion from a thing is preoccupation with it. If it is intentional, it is the locus of obligation; if it is without intention, like His saying about the embroidered garment, "it just now diverted me from my prayer," its bearer is excused, and it is a kind of forgetfulness.

In the hadith, "he was distracted from the child" means he was oblivious to him. It is said "lahā bi-l-shay'" meaning he became occupied with it, and "lahā ʿanhu" when he turned away from it. Play (lahw) belongs to the heart, and sport (laʿib) to the limbs, which is why they are combined. For this reason, His saying ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾ is more forceful in blame than "preoccupies you," for the worker may employ his limbs in what he does while his heart is not diverted by it.

So diversion is heedlessness and aversion, and "takathur" is a reciprocal form from "kathra" (abundance), that is, each of you competing with another in abundance. He leaves unspecified the thing one competes in, intending its generality and comprehensiveness: everything a servant competes in with another, other than obedience to God and His Messenger and what returns to him with benefit for his final destination, falls under this competition. So competition in anything, whether wealth, standing, leadership, women, talk, or knowledge, especially when it is not needed, and competition in books, compositions, multiplying questions, and branching and generating them, is included.

Competition is that a man seeks to be more than another, and this is blameworthy except in what brings one nearer to God; competition in that is rivalry in good deeds and racing toward them.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, that he came to the Prophet while he was reciting ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾, and he said: "The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth.' Do you have of your wealth anything but what you gave in charity and so passed on, or ate and so consumed, or wore and so wore out?"

(Benefit)
The levels are three: the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin), which is obtained from report; then the reality of what is reported becomes manifest to the heart or sight, until knowledge of it becomes the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqin); then one experiences and encounters it, and it becomes the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). Our knowledge of Paradise and Hell now is knowledge of certainty. When Paradise is brought near to the God-fearing at the Standing, and Hellfire is made manifest to the deluded, and they witness both directly, that becomes the eye of certainty, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire; then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ [al-Takathur: 6–7]. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, that is the truth of certainty.

(Section)
Qatadah said: "Two words for which the first and the last will be questioned: What were you worshipping? And what did you answer the messengers?" So He asks about the object of worship and about the worship itself.

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾ [al-Takathur: 8].

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: God, exalted is He, says: "Then God will surely ask you about the bounty you were in during the world: what did you do with it? From where did you enter into it? On what did you obtain it? And what did you do with it?"

Qatadah said: "Indeed God questions every servant about what He entrusted to him of His blessing and His right."

The bounty that one is asked about is of two kinds: a kind taken from its lawful source and spent in its proper right, for which he is asked about his gratitude; and a kind taken from an unlawful source and spent in other than its right, for which he is asked about its extraction and its disposal.

If the servant is questioned and held to account for everything, even for his hearing, sight, and heart, as He said: ﴿Indeed the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of those will be asked about﴾ [al-Isra: 36], then he is worthy to hold himself to account before he is called to the reckoning.

The obligation of self-accounting is indicated by His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear God, and let every soul look to what it has sent forward for tomorrow﴾ [al-Hashr: 18]. He, exalted is He, says: let each of you look at what he has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection of deeds: of the righteous deeds that will save him, or of the evil deeds that will destroy him.

Qatadah said: "Your Lord has never ceased bringing the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow."

The point is that the soul's soundness lies in self-accounting, and its corruption in neglecting it and yielding to it.

(Section)
Dirhams are of four kinds:
One who acquires through obedience to God and spends in God's right: that is the best of dirhams.
And a dirham acquired through disobedience to God and spent in disobedience to God: that is the worst of dirhams.
And a dirham acquired by harming a Muslim and spent in harming a Muslim: it is likewise.
And a dirham acquired through what is permissible and spent in permissible desire: that is neither for one nor against one.

These are the roots of dirhams, and from them branch other dirhams.
Among them: a dirham acquired by right and spent in falsehood.
And a dirham acquired by falsehood and spent in right, whose spending is its expiation.
And a dirham acquired from a doubtful matter, whose expiation is that it be spent in obedience.
Just as reward, punishment, praise, and blame are tied to the expenditure of the dirham, so too they are tied to its acquisition.
Likewise, one is asked about its extractor and its disposer: from where he acquired it and on what he spent it.

(Benefit)
In the words of the early scholars there occurs the explanation of a general term by a particular instance, by way of example, not as an explanation of the word's meaning in the language. Thus the meaning is altered and made to be the lexical meaning of the word, as some of them said concerning ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾: that it is cold water in summer. He did not mean that the bounty asked about is this alone.

Likewise it has been said concerning ﴿and they withhold the small kindnesses (al-maʿun)﴾ [al-Maʿun: 7] that it is the cooking pot, the axe, and the bowl. Al-maʿun is a comprehensive term for all that one benefits from. Some of the early scholars mentioned this to the questioner by way of example and as an alert, moving from the lesser to the greater. If woe is due to one who withholds this, how much more so to one who withholds what is greater in need. And if the servant is asked about thanking for cold water, how much more about what is greater in bounty than it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 102, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, glorified is He, informed that rivalry in accumulation (al-takathur) preoccupies the people of this world and diverts them from Allah and the Last Abode, until death comes to them, and they visit the graves without death. They have not awakened from the slumber of the diversion of rivalry in accumulation.

He made the endpoint "visiting the graves" rather than "death," signifying that they are neither remaining nor settled in the graves, and that they are in them in the position of visitors, who come to them once and then depart from them, just as they were in this world, likewise visitors to it, not settled in it. The abode of settlement is either Paradise or Hellfire.

Allah, glorified is He, did not specify that in which they compete in accumulation, but left out its mention, either because what is blameworthy is the very act of competing in accumulation with something, not the thing in which one competes, as one says: "Play and amusement have preoccupied you," without mentioning what one plays and amuses oneself with; or because He intends generality, which is everything in which a servant competes with another through the means of worldly life, whether wealth, rank, slaves, female slaves, buildings, orchards, or knowledge not sought for the sake of Allah's Countenance, or deeds that do not bring one closer to Allah.

All of this is from the rivalry in accumulation that diverts from Allah and the Last Abode.

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, that he said:
"I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting ﴿Rivalry in accumulation diverts you﴾, and he said: 'The son of Adam says: My wealth, my wealth. And do you have of wealth except what you gave in charity and thus passed on, or ate and thus consumed, or wore and thus wore out?'"

Then Allah threatened those whom rivalry in accumulation diverted with an emphatic threat: when they witness that their accumulation has gone to waste as scattered dust, and they know that the worldly life with which they competed was but deception and delusion, they find the consequence of their accumulation turned against them and not in their favour, and there they lose their accumulation, just as their likes lost theirs. And there appears to them from Allah what was not in their reckoning, and the accumulation that preoccupied them from Allah and the Last Abode becomes among the greatest causes of their punishment. So they are punished by their accumulation in their worldly life, then they are punished by it in the barzakh (intermediate state), then they will be punished by it on the Day of Resurrection. Thus they are the most wretched of people by their accumulation, for it yielded them ruin rather than gain and safety. They gained nothing from their accumulation except becoming among the fewest, and they obtained nothing from their exaltation through it in this world except being joined with the lowest.

How grievous is an accumulation whose burden is so heavy, and how it brings every poverty, a wealth that attracts every destitution, and a good through which one reaches every evil! Its possessor will say when his covering is removed: ﴿O my Lord, return me, so that I may do righteousness in that which I have left behind﴾. He would say: "Would that I had sent forward for my life, and worked therein in obedience to Allah before my death." ﴿Never! It is but a word he is saying﴾, so it is said to him: ﴿Never! It is merely a word he utters﴾. He does not rely upon it, and his request for return is not answered.

Reflect on his saying first "My Lord," as he seeks help from his Lord, then he turns to the angels who were commanded to bring him before his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, and says: "Return me," and then mentions the reason for his request for return, which is that he may act righteously in what he left behind of his wealth, rank, authority, strength and means. So it is said to him, "Never," there is no path for you to return, for you were given life long enough for whoever would remember to remember.

Since it is the way of the Generous, the Merciful, to answer one who asks Him for a reprieve, and to grant him an extension of time to remember what he missed, Allah, glorified is He, informed that the request of this negligent one for return is a word: he is its utterer, with no reality beneath it, and that his disposition and nature refuse to do righteousness even if he were answered. It is only something he says with his tongue, and that if he were returned he would return to what he was forbidden, and that he is indeed among the liars.

So the wisdom of the Wisest of judges, His might, His knowledge and His praise, refuses to answer him in what he asked, for there is no benefit in that. And even if he were returned, his second state would be like his first, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you could but see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say: "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers." Nay, but there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿Never! If you knew with certainty of knowledge﴾, its answer is omitted, indicated by what preceded it, meaning: "If you knew, the rivalry in accumulation would not have diverted you." This rivalry and its diversion from what is more fitting for you arose only because you lacked the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn), which is the knowledge by which its possessor reaches the level of necessities, about whose soundness and establishment one neither doubts nor disputes.

Had the reality of this knowledge reached the heart and become intimate with it, nothing would have diverted it from its requirement, and its effect would have followed upon it. For mere knowledge of the ugliness of a thing and the evil of its consequences may not suffice to abandon it. When one has the knowledge of certainty, the demand of this knowledge to abandon it becomes stronger. When it becomes the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), like the totality of direct observations, its requirement failing to follow from it becomes the rarest thing.

On this meaning Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding the people of Badr:
"We marched, and they marched toward Badr for their doom; had they known the certainty of knowledge, they would not have marched."

It was said: this is an emphasis of the attainment of knowledge, like His saying: ﴿Nay, you will come to know. Then nay, you will come to know﴾.

It was said: it is not an emphasis, rather the first knowledge is at the time of witnessing and the descent of death, and the second knowledge is in the grave. This is the saying of al-Hasan and Muqatil, and it was narrated by Ata from Ibn Abbas.

There are several proofs for the soundness of this view.

First: that a new benefit and a foundational meaning is the original principle, and it is possible to consider it, together with the grandeur and majesty of the meaning, without disturbing eloquence.

Second: the placement of "then" (thumma) between the two knowledges, which signifies the lapse of time and gravity between the two stages.

Third: that this view corresponds to reality, for the dying person knows at the time of witnessing the truth of what he was upon, then he knows in the grave and after it that knowledge with certainty, which is above the first knowledge.

Fourth: that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and others among the early Muslims understood from the verse the punishment of the grave.

al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Sulaym al-Razi narrated to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal ibn Amr ibn Zirr, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until ﴿Rivalry in accumulation diverts you﴾ was revealed."

al-Wahidi said: meaning that the meaning of His saying: ﴿Nay, you will come to know﴾ is in the grave.

Fifth: that this corresponds to what follows it in His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire, then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. This second sight differs from the first in two respects: the first is unrestricted, while the second is restricted to "the eye of certainty"; and the first precedes, while the second follows after it.

Then He concluded the surah with an emphatic announcement, using the oath particle (waw al-qasam), the emphatic lam, and the heavy nun, concerning the question about bounty. Every person will be asked about the bounty he enjoyed in this world: did he obtain it from what is lawful and by its proper means, or not? Then, if he is cleared of this question, he will be asked another question: did he thank Allah for it, by seeking help through it in obedience to Him, or not?

The first is a question about the cause of its acquisition, and the second about the place where it was spent. As in the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the narration of Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The feet of the son of Adam will not move on the Day of Resurrection from before his Lord until he is asked about five things: about his life, how he spent it; about his youth, how he wore it out; about his wealth, from where he acquired it and where he spent it; and about what he did with what he knew."

And in it also: from Abu Barzah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his life, how he spent it; about his knowledge, what he did with it; and about his wealth, from where he acquired it and how he wore it out."

He said: this is a sound hadith.

And in it also: from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection, meaning concerning bounty, is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and quench your thirst with cold water?"

And in it also: from the hadith of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When ﴿Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the bounty﴾ was revealed, al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, what bounty will we be asked about, when it is only the two blacks: dates and water? He said: As for that, it will come to be."

He said: this is a good hadith.

And from Abu Hurairah, similar, and he said: "It is only the two blacks: the enemy is present, and our swords are on our shoulders. He said: That will indeed come to be."

His ﷺ saying, "That will indeed come to be," may mean either that bounty will come to be and befall you, or that it refers to the question, meaning that the question will fall upon that, even if it is dates and water, for it is from bounty.

This is indicated by:
His ﷺ saying in the sound hadith, when they had eaten with him fresh dates and meat, and drunk cold water: "This is from the bounty about which you will be asked on the Day of Resurrection."

So this is a question about its thanks and the fulfilment of its due.

In the Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, as if he were a sheep-like stock, and he will be made to stand before Allah, the Exalted. Allah will say: I gave you, and granted you, and bestowed My favour upon you; what did you do? He will say: O Lord, I gathered it, and multiplied it, and left it greater than it was; so return me, and I will bring it to You. When he is returned, he will have sent forward no good, and he will be taken away to the Fire."

And in it, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will say: Did I not make for you hearing, sight, wealth and children, and subject for you the livestock and the tilth, and leave you to lead and graze freely? Did you think that you would meet this day of yours? He will say: No. He will say to him: Today I forget you as you forgot Me."

He said: this is a sound hadith.

Some exegetes claimed that this address is specific to the disbelievers, and that they alone are questioned about bounty. They reported this from al-Hasan and Muqatil, and al-Wahidi chose it.

He argued with the hadith of Abu Bakr: "When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah said: Do you see the meal you ate with me in the house of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, of barley bread and meat, and dates that had been pricked, and sweet water? Do you fear that this is among the bounty about which we will be asked? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: That is only for the disbelievers," and then he recited: ﴿And do We reward any but the ungrateful?﴾

al-Wahidi said: The apparent meaning supports this view, for the entire surah is an address to the polytheists and a threat to them. The meaning also supports this view, namely that the disbelievers did not fulfil the due of the bounty upon them, since they associated others with their Lord and worshipped other than Him, so they deserve to be asked about what was bestowed upon them, as a rebuke, whether they performed what was obligatory concerning it or wasted the right of the blessing. Then they are punished for abandoning gratitude by not affirming the Benefactor's oneness.

He said: This is the meaning of the saying of Muqatil, and it is the saying of al-Hasan. He said: None is asked about bounty except the people of the Fire.

I say: Neither the wording, nor the sound Sunnah, nor the indications of reason requires restricting the address to the disbelievers. Rather, the apparent wording, the explicit Sunnah and sound inference indicate that the address is general to everyone who is described as being diverted by rivalry in accumulation. There is no basis for restricting the address to some of those so described.

This is also shown by:
The saying of the Prophet ﷺ when reciting this surah: "The son of Adam says: My wealth, my wealth; and do you have of your wealth except what you ate and thus consumed, or wore and thus wore out? — the hadith." It is in Sahih Muslim.

The one who says this may be a Muslim, and may be a disbeliever.

Also indicating this: the hadiths previously mentioned, and the questioning of the Companions to the Prophet ﷺ, and their understanding of generality, to the extent that they said to him: "What bounty will we be asked about, when it is only the two blacks?" Had the address been specific to the disbelievers, he would have clarified this to them, and said: "What concern is it of yours? It is only for the disbelievers."

So the Companions understood generality, and the hadiths are explicit in generalizing. And the one upon whom the Qur'an was revealed approved their understanding of generality.

As for the hadith of Abu Bakr which the proponents of this view cited: it is not sound. The sound hadith concerning that same incident refutes it. We quote it in its wording.

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said:
"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day or night, and found Abu Bakr and Umar, and said: What brought you out of your houses at this hour? They said: Hunger, O Messenger of Allah. He said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, that which brought you out brings me out too; rise. So they rose with him. He came to a man of the Ansar, and he was not in his house. When his wife saw him, she said: Welcome and well come. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: Where is so-and-so? She said: He has gone to fetch us sweet water. Then the Ansari came, and he looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his two companions, and said: Praise be to Allah, today I have no more honourable guests than these. He said: So he went and brought them a bunch of dates containing unripe, ripe and fully ripe dates, and said: Eat of this. Then he took the knife, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: Beware of the milch animal. So he slaughtered for them, and they ate of the sheep and of that bunch, and drank. When they were satisfied and quenched, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr and Umar: By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will surely be asked about this bounty on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your houses, and you did not return until you attained this bounty."

This sound hadith is explicit in the generality of the address, and that it is not specific to the disbelievers.

Furthermore, reality also testifies to its non-specificity, for the diversion by rivalry in accumulation occurs widely among Muslims; indeed most of them have been diverted by it. The address of the Qur'an is general to whoever it reaches, and although the first to enter it were the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it encompasses those who came after them. This is known by necessity of the religion, even though some later scholars whose opinion is not considered have disputed it.

Thus we today, and those before us and after us, are included under His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting is prescribed for you﴾ and its counterparts, just as the Companions were included in it by the necessary knowledge of the religion.

So His saying: ﴿Rivalry in accumulation diverts you﴾ is an address to everyone described by this attribute.

They are in diversion and rivalry in degrees that none can count but Allah.

If it is said: Believers are not diverted by rivalry in accumulation, and therefore they do not fall under the threat mentioned for one who is diverted by it.

It is answered: This is what caused the proponents of this view to restrict it to the disbelievers, since they could not apply it generally, and they saw that the disbelievers are more deserving of the threat, so they restricted it to them.

The reply to this: the address is to the human being as human, according to the Qur'anic manner of censuring him as human, as in His sayings: ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾, ﴿And man has always been ungrateful﴾, ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾, ﴿And man carried it; indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾, and their counterparts are many.

So man, as man, is bare of every good, of beneficial knowledge and righteous deed; it is Allah, glorified is He, who perfects him therewith and gives it to him, and he has it not from himself. Rather he has from himself only ignorance, which is opposed to knowledge, and injustice, which is opposed to justice; and every knowledge, justice and good in him is from his Lord, not from himself. So diversion by rivalry in accumulation is his nature and disposition, which belong to him from himself. He can only exit it through Allah's purification of him, and making him desire the Hereafter, preferring it over rivalry in worldly accumulation. If He gives him that, well and good; otherwise he will surely be occupied with rivalry in accumulation in this world.

As for their argument from the threat for restricting the address to the disbelievers:

It is said: the threat mentioned is shared, and it is the knowledge at the witnessing of the Hereafter.

This is something that occurs to everyone, which was not present to him in this world. And His saying: ﴿You will come to know﴾ does not necessitate entering the Fire, let alone eternal abiding in it. Likewise, seeing Hellfire does not entail entering it for everyone who sees it, for the people of the standing place see it and witness it directly, and the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, has sworn that all creatures must see it, believers and disbelievers, pious and wicked: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it; that is a decree decreed by your Lord﴾.

So there is nothing in the whole of this surah that negates the generality of its address.

As for what they reported from al-Hasan: None is asked about bounty except the people of the Fire. This is false beyond doubt, either upon him or from him. And the sound explicit hadiths reject it. And with Allah is success.

It is not hidden that a surah like this, with its great significance and severe warning, and what it contains of warning the human being against diverting rivalry in accumulation, and whose meaning applies to most of creation, refuses to restrict it from beginning to end to the disbelievers, and such restriction does not befit it.

It is sufficient in this to reflect upon the elevated (marfu') hadiths concerning it. And Allah knows best.

Reflect also upon this reproach that returns to one who persisted in the diversion of rivalry in accumulation throughout his entire life, until he visited the graves, and did not awaken from the sleep of diversion, rather rivalry in accumulation put his heart to sleep, so that he did not come to himself until he was in the army of the dead.

Compare this with the condition of most of creation, and it becomes clear to you that generality is intended.

And reflect on His making the blame and threat attach to rivalry in accumulation in its absolute sense, without restriction to what is competed in, so that it includes rivalry through all the means of worldly life, with their differing kinds and types.

And moreover, "competition in increase" (al-takathur) is a reciprocal form (tafa'ul), meaning that each of the ones competing in abundance seeks to outdo his fellow. So he strives to have more than him in that by which he competes. What drives him to this is his imagination that honour belongs to the one who outdoes others, as it has been said:

"You are not the richest among them,
but honour belongs to the one who outdoes."

Had abundance come to him without competing, it would not have harmed him, just as abundance was present with a group of the Companions and did not harm them, since they did not compete with it. Whoever competes with a person in his worldly life, or his standing, or other things, his competition distracts him from competing with the people of the Hereafter.

Noble, lofty souls with high aspirations compete only in that whose benefit endures for them, through which they are perfected, purified, and become successful. They do not love that others should outdo them in this, or rival them in this competition, or race ahead of them to it. This is the competition that is the ultimate happiness of the servant.

Its opposite is the competition of the people of this world in the means of their worldly life. This is a competition that diverts them from God and from the Last Abode, and it leads toward the ultimate scarcity.

The outcome of this competition is: scarcity, poverty, and deprivation.

Competition in the means of otherworldly happiness is a competition that continually reminds one of God and His blessings. Its outcome is lasting abundance, which does not cease and does not perish. The person who engages in this competition cannot bear to see another surpass him in speech, excel him in deed, or exceed him in knowledge. When he sees someone else exceeding him in a quality of goodness, in which he is unable to catch up, he outdoes him in another quality, being capable of competing in it. This competition is not blameworthy, nor does it harm the sincerity of the servant; rather, it is the reality of rivalry and racing toward good deeds.

This was the condition of the Aws with the Khazraj, may God be pleased with them, in their rivalry before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and in each one's competing with the other in the means of pleasing and supporting him.

Likewise was the condition of ʿUmar with Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them both. When it became clear to ʿUmar how far Abu Bakr had surpassed him, he said: "By God, I will never race you to anything again."

(Benefit)
Whoever is preoccupied and diverted by competition in any matter from God and the Last Abode falls under the ruling of this verse.

Among people there is one whom competition in wealth diverts,
and another whom competition in standing or knowledge diverts, so that he gathers it for the sake of rivalry and boasting.

This latter is worse in condition before God than one who competes in wealth and standing, for he has made the means of the Hereafter serve the world, whereas the owner of wealth and standing has employed the means of the world for it and competed with its means.

(Section)
Whoever reflects on the fine placement of "kalla" (no!) in this position will find that it contains a rebuke to them, a warning against competition, and a negation and nullification of what they hope for from the benefit of competition, their honour, and their perfection through it. The word thus contains both prohibition and negation. God, glorified is He, informs them that they will surely come to know the outcome of their competition, knowledge after knowledge, and that they will surely see the abode of those who competed in worldly things, which diverted them from the Hereafter, sight after sight. He, glorified is He, will surely ask them about the sources of their competition: from where did they extract them, and on what did they spend them?

How magnificent is this surah, how sublime and greatest in benefit, most eloquent in admonition and warning, and most intense in encouragement toward the Hereafter and in discouragement from this world, despite its extreme brevity, the force of its wording, and the beauty of its composition. Blessed is He who spoke it in truth and conveyed it to His Messenger as revelation.

(Section)
Consider how, upon reaching the end of every living thing, He made them visitors, not residents. Rather, they are deposited in graves for a period, and before them lies the abode of settlement. If they are visitors upon reaching the end, how much more so while they are on the road in this abode? They are therefore passers-by on a path toward the place of visitation, and then they move from the place of visitation to the place of settlement.

So here there are three matters: passing along the path in this world, its goal being the visiting of graves, and after that the transfer to the abode of settlement.

(Benefit)
The Almighty's saying: ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾ to its end.

This surah was devoted to promise, threat, and warning, and it suffices as admonition for whoever understands it.

His saying ﴿diverts you﴾ means: occupies you in a way for which you have no excuse. Diversion from a thing is preoccupation with it. If it is intentional, it is the locus of obligation; if it is without intention, like His saying about the embroidered garment, "it just now diverted me from my prayer," its bearer is excused, and it is a kind of forgetfulness.

In the hadith, "he was distracted from the child" means he was oblivious to him. It is said "lahā bi-l-shay'" meaning he became occupied with it, and "lahā ʿanhu" when he turned away from it. Play (lahw) belongs to the heart, and sport (laʿib) to the limbs, which is why they are combined. For this reason, His saying ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾ is more forceful in blame than "preoccupies you," for the worker may employ his limbs in what he does while his heart is not diverted by it.

So diversion is heedlessness and aversion, and "takathur" is a reciprocal form from "kathra" (abundance), that is, each of you competing with another in abundance. He leaves unspecified the thing one competes in, intending its generality and comprehensiveness: everything a servant competes in with another, other than obedience to God and His Messenger and what returns to him with benefit for his final destination, falls under this competition. So competition in anything, whether wealth, standing, leadership, women, talk, or knowledge, especially when it is not needed, and competition in books, compositions, multiplying questions, and branching and generating them, is included.

Competition is that a man seeks to be more than another, and this is blameworthy except in what brings one nearer to God; competition in that is rivalry in good deeds and racing toward them.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, that he came to the Prophet while he was reciting ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾, and he said: "The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth.' Do you have of your wealth anything but what you gave in charity and so passed on, or ate and so consumed, or wore and so wore out?"

(Benefit)
The levels are three: the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin), which is obtained from report; then the reality of what is reported becomes manifest to the heart or sight, until knowledge of it becomes the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqin); then one experiences and encounters it, and it becomes the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). Our knowledge of Paradise and Hell now is knowledge of certainty. When Paradise is brought near to the God-fearing at the Standing, and Hellfire is made manifest to the deluded, and they witness both directly, that becomes the eye of certainty, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire; then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ [al-Takathur: 6–7]. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, that is the truth of certainty.

(Section)
Qatadah said: "Two words for which the first and the last will be questioned: What were you worshipping? And what did you answer the messengers?" So He asks about the object of worship and about the worship itself.

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾ [al-Takathur: 8].

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: God, exalted is He, says: "Then God will surely ask you about the bounty you were in during the world: what did you do with it? From where did you enter into it? On what did you obtain it? And what did you do with it?"

Qatadah said: "Indeed God questions every servant about what He entrusted to him of His blessing and His right."

The bounty that one is asked about is of two kinds: a kind taken from its lawful source and spent in its proper right, for which he is asked about his gratitude; and a kind taken from an unlawful source and spent in other than its right, for which he is asked about its extraction and its disposal.

If the servant is questioned and held to account for everything, even for his hearing, sight, and heart, as He said: ﴿Indeed the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of those will be asked about﴾ [al-Isra: 36], then he is worthy to hold himself to account before he is called to the reckoning.

The obligation of self-accounting is indicated by His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear God, and let every soul look to what it has sent forward for tomorrow﴾ [al-Hashr: 18]. He, exalted is He, says: let each of you look at what he has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection of deeds: of the righteous deeds that will save him, or of the evil deeds that will destroy him.

Qatadah said: "Your Lord has never ceased bringing the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow."

The point is that the soul's soundness lies in self-accounting, and its corruption in neglecting it and yielding to it.

(Section)
Dirhams are of four kinds:
One who acquires through obedience to God and spends in God's right: that is the best of dirhams.
And a dirham acquired through disobedience to God and spent in disobedience to God: that is the worst of dirhams.
And a dirham acquired by harming a Muslim and spent in harming a Muslim: it is likewise.
And a dirham acquired through what is permissible and spent in permissible desire: that is neither for one nor against one.

These are the roots of dirhams, and from them branch other dirhams.
Among them: a dirham acquired by right and spent in falsehood.
And a dirham acquired by falsehood and spent in right, whose spending is its expiation.
And a dirham acquired from a doubtful matter, whose expiation is that it be spent in obedience.
Just as reward, punishment, praise, and blame are tied to the expenditure of the dirham, so too they are tied to its acquisition.
Likewise, one is asked about its extractor and its disposer: from where he acquired it and on what he spent it.

(Benefit)
In the words of the early scholars there occurs the explanation of a general term by a particular instance, by way of example, not as an explanation of the word's meaning in the language. Thus the meaning is altered and made to be the lexical meaning of the word, as some of them said concerning ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾: that it is cold water in summer. He did not mean that the bounty asked about is this alone.

Likewise it has been said concerning ﴿and they withhold the small kindnesses (al-maʿun)﴾ [al-Maʿun: 7] that it is the cooking pot, the axe, and the bowl. Al-maʿun is a comprehensive term for all that one benefits from. Some of the early scholars mentioned this to the questioner by way of example and as an alert, moving from the lesser to the greater. If woe is due to one who withholds this, how much more so to one who withholds what is greater in need. And if the servant is asked about thanking for cold water, how much more about what is greater in bounty than it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 102, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, glorified is He, informed that rivalry in accumulation (al-takathur) preoccupies the people of this world and diverts them from Allah and the Last Abode, until death comes to them, and they visit the graves without death. They have not awakened from the slumber of the diversion of rivalry in accumulation.

He made the endpoint "visiting the graves" rather than "death," signifying that they are neither remaining nor settled in the graves, and that they are in them in the position of visitors, who come to them once and then depart from them, just as they were in this world, likewise visitors to it, not settled in it. The abode of settlement is either Paradise or Hellfire.

Allah, glorified is He, did not specify that in which they compete in accumulation, but left out its mention, either because what is blameworthy is the very act of competing in accumulation with something, not the thing in which one competes, as one says: "Play and amusement have preoccupied you," without mentioning what one plays and amuses oneself with; or because He intends generality, which is everything in which a servant competes with another through the means of worldly life, whether wealth, rank, slaves, female slaves, buildings, orchards, or knowledge not sought for the sake of Allah's Countenance, or deeds that do not bring one closer to Allah.

All of this is from the rivalry in accumulation that diverts from Allah and the Last Abode.

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, that he said:
"I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting ﴿Rivalry in accumulation diverts you﴾, and he said: 'The son of Adam says: My wealth, my wealth. And do you have of wealth except what you gave in charity and thus passed on, or ate and thus consumed, or wore and thus wore out?'"

Then Allah threatened those whom rivalry in accumulation diverted with an emphatic threat: when they witness that their accumulation has gone to waste as scattered dust, and they know that the worldly life with which they competed was but deception and delusion, they find the consequence of their accumulation turned against them and not in their favour, and there they lose their accumulation, just as their likes lost theirs. And there appears to them from Allah what was not in their reckoning, and the accumulation that preoccupied them from Allah and the Last Abode becomes among the greatest causes of their punishment. So they are punished by their accumulation in their worldly life, then they are punished by it in the barzakh (intermediate state), then they will be punished by it on the Day of Resurrection. Thus they are the most wretched of people by their accumulation, for it yielded them ruin rather than gain and safety. They gained nothing from their accumulation except becoming among the fewest, and they obtained nothing from their exaltation through it in this world except being joined with the lowest.

How grievous is an accumulation whose burden is so heavy, and how it brings every poverty, a wealth that attracts every destitution, and a good through which one reaches every evil! Its possessor will say when his covering is removed: ﴿O my Lord, return me, so that I may do righteousness in that which I have left behind﴾. He would say: "Would that I had sent forward for my life, and worked therein in obedience to Allah before my death." ﴿Never! It is but a word he is saying﴾, so it is said to him: ﴿Never! It is merely a word he utters﴾. He does not rely upon it, and his request for return is not answered.

Reflect on his saying first "My Lord," as he seeks help from his Lord, then he turns to the angels who were commanded to bring him before his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, and says: "Return me," and then mentions the reason for his request for return, which is that he may act righteously in what he left behind of his wealth, rank, authority, strength and means. So it is said to him, "Never," there is no path for you to return, for you were given life long enough for whoever would remember to remember.

Since it is the way of the Generous, the Merciful, to answer one who asks Him for a reprieve, and to grant him an extension of time to remember what he missed, Allah, glorified is He, informed that the request of this negligent one for return is a word: he is its utterer, with no reality beneath it, and that his disposition and nature refuse to do righteousness even if he were answered. It is only something he says with his tongue, and that if he were returned he would return to what he was forbidden, and that he is indeed among the liars.

So the wisdom of the Wisest of judges, His might, His knowledge and His praise, refuses to answer him in what he asked, for there is no benefit in that. And even if he were returned, his second state would be like his first, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you could but see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say: "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers." Nay, but there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿Never! If you knew with certainty of knowledge﴾, its answer is omitted, indicated by what preceded it, meaning: "If you knew, the rivalry in accumulation would not have diverted you." This rivalry and its diversion from what is more fitting for you arose only because you lacked the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn), which is the knowledge by which its possessor reaches the level of necessities, about whose soundness and establishment one neither doubts nor disputes.

Had the reality of this knowledge reached the heart and become intimate with it, nothing would have diverted it from its requirement, and its effect would have followed upon it. For mere knowledge of the ugliness of a thing and the evil of its consequences may not suffice to abandon it. When one has the knowledge of certainty, the demand of this knowledge to abandon it becomes stronger. When it becomes the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), like the totality of direct observations, its requirement failing to follow from it becomes the rarest thing.

On this meaning Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding the people of Badr:
"We marched, and they marched toward Badr for their doom; had they known the certainty of knowledge, they would not have marched."

It was said: this is an emphasis of the attainment of knowledge, like His saying: ﴿Nay, you will come to know. Then nay, you will come to know﴾.

It was said: it is not an emphasis, rather the first knowledge is at the time of witnessing and the descent of death, and the second knowledge is in the grave. This is the saying of al-Hasan and Muqatil, and it was narrated by Ata from Ibn Abbas.

There are several proofs for the soundness of this view.

First: that a new benefit and a foundational meaning is the original principle, and it is possible to consider it, together with the grandeur and majesty of the meaning, without disturbing eloquence.

Second: the placement of "then" (thumma) between the two knowledges, which signifies the lapse of time and gravity between the two stages.

Third: that this view corresponds to reality, for the dying person knows at the time of witnessing the truth of what he was upon, then he knows in the grave and after it that knowledge with certainty, which is above the first knowledge.

Fourth: that Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, and others among the early Muslims understood from the verse the punishment of the grave.

al-Tirmidhi said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Hakkam ibn Sulaym al-Razi narrated to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Hajjaj ibn Minhal ibn Amr ibn Zirr, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We continued to doubt the punishment of the grave until ﴿Rivalry in accumulation diverts you﴾ was revealed."

al-Wahidi said: meaning that the meaning of His saying: ﴿Nay, you will come to know﴾ is in the grave.

Fifth: that this corresponds to what follows it in His saying: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire, then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾. This second sight differs from the first in two respects: the first is unrestricted, while the second is restricted to "the eye of certainty"; and the first precedes, while the second follows after it.

Then He concluded the surah with an emphatic announcement, using the oath particle (waw al-qasam), the emphatic lam, and the heavy nun, concerning the question about bounty. Every person will be asked about the bounty he enjoyed in this world: did he obtain it from what is lawful and by its proper means, or not? Then, if he is cleared of this question, he will be asked another question: did he thank Allah for it, by seeking help through it in obedience to Him, or not?

The first is a question about the cause of its acquisition, and the second about the place where it was spent. As in the Jami' of al-Tirmidhi, from the narration of Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The feet of the son of Adam will not move on the Day of Resurrection from before his Lord until he is asked about five things: about his life, how he spent it; about his youth, how he wore it out; about his wealth, from where he acquired it and where he spent it; and about what he did with what he knew."

And in it also: from Abu Barzah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The feet of a servant will not move on the Day of Resurrection until he is asked about his life, how he spent it; about his knowledge, what he did with it; and about his wealth, from where he acquired it and how he wore it out."

He said: this is a sound hadith.

And in it also: from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing a servant will be asked about on the Day of Resurrection, meaning concerning bounty, is that it will be said to him: Did We not make your body healthy, and quench your thirst with cold water?"

And in it also: from the hadith of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When ﴿Then you will surely be asked on that Day about the bounty﴾ was revealed, al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, what bounty will we be asked about, when it is only the two blacks: dates and water? He said: As for that, it will come to be."

He said: this is a good hadith.

And from Abu Hurairah, similar, and he said: "It is only the two blacks: the enemy is present, and our swords are on our shoulders. He said: That will indeed come to be."

His ﷺ saying, "That will indeed come to be," may mean either that bounty will come to be and befall you, or that it refers to the question, meaning that the question will fall upon that, even if it is dates and water, for it is from bounty.

This is indicated by:
His ﷺ saying in the sound hadith, when they had eaten with him fresh dates and meat, and drunk cold water: "This is from the bounty about which you will be asked on the Day of Resurrection."

So this is a question about its thanks and the fulfilment of its due.

In the Tirmidhi, from the hadith of Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, as if he were a sheep-like stock, and he will be made to stand before Allah, the Exalted. Allah will say: I gave you, and granted you, and bestowed My favour upon you; what did you do? He will say: O Lord, I gathered it, and multiplied it, and left it greater than it was; so return me, and I will bring it to You. When he is returned, he will have sent forward no good, and he will be taken away to the Fire."

And in it, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id and Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A servant will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will say: Did I not make for you hearing, sight, wealth and children, and subject for you the livestock and the tilth, and leave you to lead and graze freely? Did you think that you would meet this day of yours? He will say: No. He will say to him: Today I forget you as you forgot Me."

He said: this is a sound hadith.

Some exegetes claimed that this address is specific to the disbelievers, and that they alone are questioned about bounty. They reported this from al-Hasan and Muqatil, and al-Wahidi chose it.

He argued with the hadith of Abu Bakr: "When this verse was revealed, the Messenger of Allah said: Do you see the meal you ate with me in the house of Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, of barley bread and meat, and dates that had been pricked, and sweet water? Do you fear that this is among the bounty about which we will be asked? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: That is only for the disbelievers," and then he recited: ﴿And do We reward any but the ungrateful?﴾

al-Wahidi said: The apparent meaning supports this view, for the entire surah is an address to the polytheists and a threat to them. The meaning also supports this view, namely that the disbelievers did not fulfil the due of the bounty upon them, since they associated others with their Lord and worshipped other than Him, so they deserve to be asked about what was bestowed upon them, as a rebuke, whether they performed what was obligatory concerning it or wasted the right of the blessing. Then they are punished for abandoning gratitude by not affirming the Benefactor's oneness.

He said: This is the meaning of the saying of Muqatil, and it is the saying of al-Hasan. He said: None is asked about bounty except the people of the Fire.

I say: Neither the wording, nor the sound Sunnah, nor the indications of reason requires restricting the address to the disbelievers. Rather, the apparent wording, the explicit Sunnah and sound inference indicate that the address is general to everyone who is described as being diverted by rivalry in accumulation. There is no basis for restricting the address to some of those so described.

This is also shown by:
The saying of the Prophet ﷺ when reciting this surah: "The son of Adam says: My wealth, my wealth; and do you have of your wealth except what you ate and thus consumed, or wore and thus wore out? — the hadith." It is in Sahih Muslim.

The one who says this may be a Muslim, and may be a disbeliever.

Also indicating this: the hadiths previously mentioned, and the questioning of the Companions to the Prophet ﷺ, and their understanding of generality, to the extent that they said to him: "What bounty will we be asked about, when it is only the two blacks?" Had the address been specific to the disbelievers, he would have clarified this to them, and said: "What concern is it of yours? It is only for the disbelievers."

So the Companions understood generality, and the hadiths are explicit in generalizing. And the one upon whom the Qur'an was revealed approved their understanding of generality.

As for the hadith of Abu Bakr which the proponents of this view cited: it is not sound. The sound hadith concerning that same incident refutes it. We quote it in its wording.

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said:
"The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out one day or night, and found Abu Bakr and Umar, and said: What brought you out of your houses at this hour? They said: Hunger, O Messenger of Allah. He said: By Him in whose hand is my soul, that which brought you out brings me out too; rise. So they rose with him. He came to a man of the Ansar, and he was not in his house. When his wife saw him, she said: Welcome and well come. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to her: Where is so-and-so? She said: He has gone to fetch us sweet water. Then the Ansari came, and he looked at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his two companions, and said: Praise be to Allah, today I have no more honourable guests than these. He said: So he went and brought them a bunch of dates containing unripe, ripe and fully ripe dates, and said: Eat of this. Then he took the knife, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: Beware of the milch animal. So he slaughtered for them, and they ate of the sheep and of that bunch, and drank. When they were satisfied and quenched, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Abu Bakr and Umar: By Him in whose hand is my soul, you will surely be asked about this bounty on the Day of Resurrection. Hunger brought you out of your houses, and you did not return until you attained this bounty."

This sound hadith is explicit in the generality of the address, and that it is not specific to the disbelievers.

Furthermore, reality also testifies to its non-specificity, for the diversion by rivalry in accumulation occurs widely among Muslims; indeed most of them have been diverted by it. The address of the Qur'an is general to whoever it reaches, and although the first to enter it were the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, it encompasses those who came after them. This is known by necessity of the religion, even though some later scholars whose opinion is not considered have disputed it.

Thus we today, and those before us and after us, are included under His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, fasting is prescribed for you﴾ and its counterparts, just as the Companions were included in it by the necessary knowledge of the religion.

So His saying: ﴿Rivalry in accumulation diverts you﴾ is an address to everyone described by this attribute.

They are in diversion and rivalry in degrees that none can count but Allah.

If it is said: Believers are not diverted by rivalry in accumulation, and therefore they do not fall under the threat mentioned for one who is diverted by it.

It is answered: This is what caused the proponents of this view to restrict it to the disbelievers, since they could not apply it generally, and they saw that the disbelievers are more deserving of the threat, so they restricted it to them.

The reply to this: the address is to the human being as human, according to the Qur'anic manner of censuring him as human, as in His sayings: ﴿And man has always been hasty﴾, ﴿And man has always been ungrateful﴾, ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful to his Lord﴾, ﴿And man carried it; indeed he was a wrongdoer, ignorant﴾, ﴿Indeed, man is ungrateful﴾, and their counterparts are many.

So man, as man, is bare of every good, of beneficial knowledge and righteous deed; it is Allah, glorified is He, who perfects him therewith and gives it to him, and he has it not from himself. Rather he has from himself only ignorance, which is opposed to knowledge, and injustice, which is opposed to justice; and every knowledge, justice and good in him is from his Lord, not from himself. So diversion by rivalry in accumulation is his nature and disposition, which belong to him from himself. He can only exit it through Allah's purification of him, and making him desire the Hereafter, preferring it over rivalry in worldly accumulation. If He gives him that, well and good; otherwise he will surely be occupied with rivalry in accumulation in this world.

As for their argument from the threat for restricting the address to the disbelievers:

It is said: the threat mentioned is shared, and it is the knowledge at the witnessing of the Hereafter.

This is something that occurs to everyone, which was not present to him in this world. And His saying: ﴿You will come to know﴾ does not necessitate entering the Fire, let alone eternal abiding in it. Likewise, seeing Hellfire does not entail entering it for everyone who sees it, for the people of the standing place see it and witness it directly, and the Lord, blessed and exalted is He, has sworn that all creatures must see it, believers and disbelievers, pious and wicked: ﴿And there is none of you but will pass over it; that is a decree decreed by your Lord﴾.

So there is nothing in the whole of this surah that negates the generality of its address.

As for what they reported from al-Hasan: None is asked about bounty except the people of the Fire. This is false beyond doubt, either upon him or from him. And the sound explicit hadiths reject it. And with Allah is success.

It is not hidden that a surah like this, with its great significance and severe warning, and what it contains of warning the human being against diverting rivalry in accumulation, and whose meaning applies to most of creation, refuses to restrict it from beginning to end to the disbelievers, and such restriction does not befit it.

It is sufficient in this to reflect upon the elevated (marfu') hadiths concerning it. And Allah knows best.

Reflect also upon this reproach that returns to one who persisted in the diversion of rivalry in accumulation throughout his entire life, until he visited the graves, and did not awaken from the sleep of diversion, rather rivalry in accumulation put his heart to sleep, so that he did not come to himself until he was in the army of the dead.

Compare this with the condition of most of creation, and it becomes clear to you that generality is intended.

And reflect on His making the blame and threat attach to rivalry in accumulation in its absolute sense, without restriction to what is competed in, so that it includes rivalry through all the means of worldly life, with their differing kinds and types.

And moreover, "competition in increase" (al-takathur) is a reciprocal form (tafa'ul), meaning that each of the ones competing in abundance seeks to outdo his fellow. So he strives to have more than him in that by which he competes. What drives him to this is his imagination that honour belongs to the one who outdoes others, as it has been said:

"You are not the richest among them,
but honour belongs to the one who outdoes."

Had abundance come to him without competing, it would not have harmed him, just as abundance was present with a group of the Companions and did not harm them, since they did not compete with it. Whoever competes with a person in his worldly life, or his standing, or other things, his competition distracts him from competing with the people of the Hereafter.

Noble, lofty souls with high aspirations compete only in that whose benefit endures for them, through which they are perfected, purified, and become successful. They do not love that others should outdo them in this, or rival them in this competition, or race ahead of them to it. This is the competition that is the ultimate happiness of the servant.

Its opposite is the competition of the people of this world in the means of their worldly life. This is a competition that diverts them from God and from the Last Abode, and it leads toward the ultimate scarcity.

The outcome of this competition is: scarcity, poverty, and deprivation.

Competition in the means of otherworldly happiness is a competition that continually reminds one of God and His blessings. Its outcome is lasting abundance, which does not cease and does not perish. The person who engages in this competition cannot bear to see another surpass him in speech, excel him in deed, or exceed him in knowledge. When he sees someone else exceeding him in a quality of goodness, in which he is unable to catch up, he outdoes him in another quality, being capable of competing in it. This competition is not blameworthy, nor does it harm the sincerity of the servant; rather, it is the reality of rivalry and racing toward good deeds.

This was the condition of the Aws with the Khazraj, may God be pleased with them, in their rivalry before the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and in each one's competing with the other in the means of pleasing and supporting him.

Likewise was the condition of ʿUmar with Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with them both. When it became clear to ʿUmar how far Abu Bakr had surpassed him, he said: "By God, I will never race you to anything again."

(Benefit)
Whoever is preoccupied and diverted by competition in any matter from God and the Last Abode falls under the ruling of this verse.

Among people there is one whom competition in wealth diverts,
and another whom competition in standing or knowledge diverts, so that he gathers it for the sake of rivalry and boasting.

This latter is worse in condition before God than one who competes in wealth and standing, for he has made the means of the Hereafter serve the world, whereas the owner of wealth and standing has employed the means of the world for it and competed with its means.

(Section)
Whoever reflects on the fine placement of "kalla" (no!) in this position will find that it contains a rebuke to them, a warning against competition, and a negation and nullification of what they hope for from the benefit of competition, their honour, and their perfection through it. The word thus contains both prohibition and negation. God, glorified is He, informs them that they will surely come to know the outcome of their competition, knowledge after knowledge, and that they will surely see the abode of those who competed in worldly things, which diverted them from the Hereafter, sight after sight. He, glorified is He, will surely ask them about the sources of their competition: from where did they extract them, and on what did they spend them?

How magnificent is this surah, how sublime and greatest in benefit, most eloquent in admonition and warning, and most intense in encouragement toward the Hereafter and in discouragement from this world, despite its extreme brevity, the force of its wording, and the beauty of its composition. Blessed is He who spoke it in truth and conveyed it to His Messenger as revelation.

(Section)
Consider how, upon reaching the end of every living thing, He made them visitors, not residents. Rather, they are deposited in graves for a period, and before them lies the abode of settlement. If they are visitors upon reaching the end, how much more so while they are on the road in this abode? They are therefore passers-by on a path toward the place of visitation, and then they move from the place of visitation to the place of settlement.

So here there are three matters: passing along the path in this world, its goal being the visiting of graves, and after that the transfer to the abode of settlement.

(Benefit)
The Almighty's saying: ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾ to its end.

This surah was devoted to promise, threat, and warning, and it suffices as admonition for whoever understands it.

His saying ﴿diverts you﴾ means: occupies you in a way for which you have no excuse. Diversion from a thing is preoccupation with it. If it is intentional, it is the locus of obligation; if it is without intention, like His saying about the embroidered garment, "it just now diverted me from my prayer," its bearer is excused, and it is a kind of forgetfulness.

In the hadith, "he was distracted from the child" means he was oblivious to him. It is said "lahā bi-l-shay'" meaning he became occupied with it, and "lahā ʿanhu" when he turned away from it. Play (lahw) belongs to the heart, and sport (laʿib) to the limbs, which is why they are combined. For this reason, His saying ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾ is more forceful in blame than "preoccupies you," for the worker may employ his limbs in what he does while his heart is not diverted by it.

So diversion is heedlessness and aversion, and "takathur" is a reciprocal form from "kathra" (abundance), that is, each of you competing with another in abundance. He leaves unspecified the thing one competes in, intending its generality and comprehensiveness: everything a servant competes in with another, other than obedience to God and His Messenger and what returns to him with benefit for his final destination, falls under this competition. So competition in anything, whether wealth, standing, leadership, women, talk, or knowledge, especially when it is not needed, and competition in books, compositions, multiplying questions, and branching and generating them, is included.

Competition is that a man seeks to be more than another, and this is blameworthy except in what brings one nearer to God; competition in that is rivalry in good deeds and racing toward them.

In Sahih Muslim, from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, that he came to the Prophet while he was reciting ﴿Your competition in increase diverts you﴾, and he said: "The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth.' Do you have of your wealth anything but what you gave in charity and so passed on, or ate and so consumed, or wore and so wore out?"

(Benefit)
The levels are three: the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin), which is obtained from report; then the reality of what is reported becomes manifest to the heart or sight, until knowledge of it becomes the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqin); then one experiences and encounters it, and it becomes the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin). Our knowledge of Paradise and Hell now is knowledge of certainty. When Paradise is brought near to the God-fearing at the Standing, and Hellfire is made manifest to the deluded, and they witness both directly, that becomes the eye of certainty, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿You will surely see the Hellfire; then you will surely see it with the eye of certainty﴾ [al-Takathur: 6–7]. When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, that is the truth of certainty.

(Section)
Qatadah said: "Two words for which the first and the last will be questioned: What were you worshipping? And what did you answer the messengers?" So He asks about the object of worship and about the worship itself.

And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾ [al-Takathur: 8].

Muhammad ibn Jarir said: God, exalted is He, says: "Then God will surely ask you about the bounty you were in during the world: what did you do with it? From where did you enter into it? On what did you obtain it? And what did you do with it?"

Qatadah said: "Indeed God questions every servant about what He entrusted to him of His blessing and His right."

The bounty that one is asked about is of two kinds: a kind taken from its lawful source and spent in its proper right, for which he is asked about his gratitude; and a kind taken from an unlawful source and spent in other than its right, for which he is asked about its extraction and its disposal.

If the servant is questioned and held to account for everything, even for his hearing, sight, and heart, as He said: ﴿Indeed the hearing and the sight and the heart, all of those will be asked about﴾ [al-Isra: 36], then he is worthy to hold himself to account before he is called to the reckoning.

The obligation of self-accounting is indicated by His saying: ﴿O you who believe, fear God, and let every soul look to what it has sent forward for tomorrow﴾ [al-Hashr: 18]. He, exalted is He, says: let each of you look at what he has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection of deeds: of the righteous deeds that will save him, or of the evil deeds that will destroy him.

Qatadah said: "Your Lord has never ceased bringing the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow."

The point is that the soul's soundness lies in self-accounting, and its corruption in neglecting it and yielding to it.

(Section)
Dirhams are of four kinds:
One who acquires through obedience to God and spends in God's right: that is the best of dirhams.
And a dirham acquired through disobedience to God and spent in disobedience to God: that is the worst of dirhams.
And a dirham acquired by harming a Muslim and spent in harming a Muslim: it is likewise.
And a dirham acquired through what is permissible and spent in permissible desire: that is neither for one nor against one.

These are the roots of dirhams, and from them branch other dirhams.
Among them: a dirham acquired by right and spent in falsehood.
And a dirham acquired by falsehood and spent in right, whose spending is its expiation.
And a dirham acquired from a doubtful matter, whose expiation is that it be spent in obedience.
Just as reward, punishment, praise, and blame are tied to the expenditure of the dirham, so too they are tied to its acquisition.
Likewise, one is asked about its extractor and its disposer: from where he acquired it and on what he spent it.

(Benefit)
In the words of the early scholars there occurs the explanation of a general term by a particular instance, by way of example, not as an explanation of the word's meaning in the language. Thus the meaning is altered and made to be the lexical meaning of the word, as some of them said concerning ﴿Then you will surely be asked that Day about the bounty﴾: that it is cold water in summer. He did not mean that the bounty asked about is this alone.

Likewise it has been said concerning ﴿and they withhold the small kindnesses (al-maʿun)﴾ [al-Maʿun: 7] that it is the cooking pot, the axe, and the bowl. Al-maʿun is a comprehensive term for all that one benefits from. Some of the early scholars mentioned this to the questioner by way of example and as an alert, moving from the lesser to the greater. If woe is due to one who withholds this, how much more so to one who withholds what is greater in need. And if the servant is asked about thanking for cold water, how much more about what is greater in bounty than it.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 102, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Allah, glorified is He, informed that rivalry in accumulation (al-takathur) preoccupies the people of this world and diverts them from Allah and the Last Abode, until death comes to them, and they visit the graves without death. They have not awakened from the slumber of the diversion of rivalry in accumulation.

He made the endpoint "visiting the graves" rather than "death," signifying that they are neither remaining nor settled in the graves, and that they are in them in the position of visitors, who come to them once and then depart from them, just as they were in this world, likewise visitors to it, not settled in it. The abode of settlement is either Paradise or Hellfire.

Allah, glorified is He, did not specify that in which they compete in accumulation, but left out its mention, either because what is blameworthy is the very act of competing in accumulation with something, not the thing in which one competes, as one says: "Play and amusement have preoccupied you," without mentioning what one plays and amuses oneself with; or because He intends generality, which is everything in which a servant competes with another through the means of worldly life, whether wealth, rank, slaves, female slaves, buildings, orchards, or knowledge not sought for the sake of Allah's Countenance, or deeds that do not bring one closer to Allah.

All of this is from the rivalry in accumulation that diverts from Allah and the Last Abode.

In Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abdullah ibn al-Shikhkhir, that he said:
"I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting ﴿Rivalry in accumulation diverts you﴾, and he said: 'The son of Adam says: My wealth, my wealth. And do you have of wealth except what you gave in charity and thus passed on, or ate and thus consumed, or wore and thus wore out?'"

Then Allah threatened those whom rivalry in accumulation diverted with an emphatic threat: when they witness that their accumulation has gone to waste as scattered dust, and they know that the worldly life with which they competed was but deception and delusion, they find the consequence of their accumulation turned against them and not in their favour, and there they lose their accumulation, just as their likes lost theirs. And there appears to them from Allah what was not in their reckoning, and the accumulation that preoccupied them from Allah and the Last Abode becomes among the greatest causes of their punishment. So they are punished by their accumulation in their worldly life, then they are punished by it in the barzakh (intermediate state), then they will be punished by it on the Day of Resurrection. Thus they are the most wretched of people by their accumulation, for it yielded them ruin rather than gain and safety. They gained nothing from their accumulation except becoming among the fewest, and they obtained nothing from their exaltation through it in this world except being joined with the lowest.

How grievous is an accumulation whose burden is so heavy, and how it brings every poverty, a wealth that attracts every destitution, and a good through which one reaches every evil! Its possessor will say when his covering is removed: ﴿O my Lord, return me, so that I may do righteousness in that which I have left behind﴾. He would say: "Would that I had sent forward for my life, and worked therein in obedience to Allah before my death." ﴿Never! It is but a word he is saying﴾, so it is said to him: ﴿Never! It is merely a word he utters﴾. He does not rely upon it, and his request for return is not answered.

Reflect on his saying first "My Lord," as he seeks help from his Lord, then he turns to the angels who were commanded to bring him before his Lord, blessed and exalted is He, and says: "Return me," and then mentions the reason for his request for return, which is that he may act righteously in what he left behind of his wealth, rank, authority, strength and means. So it is said to him, "Never," there is no path for you to return, for you were given life long enough for whoever would remember to remember.

Since it is the way of the Generous, the Merciful, to answer one who asks Him for a reprieve, and to grant him an extension of time to remember what he missed, Allah, glorified is He, informed that the request of this negligent one for return is a word: he is its utterer, with no reality beneath it, and that his disposition and nature refuse to do righteousness even if he were answered. It is only something he says with his tongue, and that if he were returned he would return to what he was forbidden, and that he is indeed among the liars.

So the wisdom of the Wisest of judges, His might, His knowledge and His praise, refuses to answer him in what he asked, for there is no benefit in that. And even if he were returned, his second state would be like his first, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿If you could but see when they are made to stand over the Fire, and they say: "Would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord, and we would be among the believers." Nay, but there has appeared to them what they used to conceal before. And even if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden﴾.

As for His saying: ﴿Never! If you knew with certainty of knowledge﴾, its answer is omitted, indicated by what preceded it, meaning: "If you knew, the rivalry in accumulation would not have diverted you." This rivalry and its diversion from what is more fitting for you arose only because you lacked the knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn), which is the knowledge by which its possessor reaches the level of necessities, about whose soundness and establishment one neither doubts nor disputes.

Had the reality of this knowledge reached the heart and become intimate with it, nothing would have diverted it from its requirement, and its effect would have followed upon it. For mere knowledge of the ugliness of a thing and the evil of its consequences may not suffice to abandon it. When one has the knowledge of certainty, the demand of this knowledge to abandon it becomes stronger.
